blocks.text: Method 1 for 1,082 Buildings - From BAG Floor Area to Material, CO2 and Estimated WOZ Value
1. Summary

This document describes Method 1 as one process: from the BAG floor area (GO) of each building, to its material mass, its embodied CO2 and its Estimated WOZ Value. Part A (steps 1-5, sections 4-9) calculates materials and CO2; part B (steps 6-10, sections 10-17) calculates the Estimated WOZ Value. Section 18 follows one building through every step.
1.1 Material and CO2

This document explains how Method 1 calculates material mass and CO2 for 1,082 buildings: 1,081 demolition buildings plus one added building, Jan Provostlaan 16 in Bilthoven. Method 1 needs one measured number per building - the gross floor area (GO) from BAG - and multiplies it by the material intensities of Tabel B2 for the building's type and age. The result is 4,335,383 tonnes of material and 1,874,724 tonnes CO2e, reported in 13 materials.
1.2 Estimated WOZ Value
Every building has an Estimated WOZ Value for WOZ year 2026 (valuation date 1 January 2025). It is a model estimate, not an official WOZ value.

blocks.text: 1.3 How to read this document
Every number is one of three kinds:
MEASURED - read directly from a BAG field (gross floor area, building type, year built).
DERIVED - calculated only from measured numbers (mass = area x intensity, CO2 = mass x factor).
ASSUMED - our own chosen value: the B2 profile per building type and age, and the emission factors.

Method 1 uses no geometry: two buildings with the same floor area, type and age get the same material estimate, whatever their shape. Method 2 is the geometry-based estimate and is described in its own document.

Where the assumptions are: every assumption has an ID. A1-A8 belong to the material and CO2 calculation (section 9); B1-B9 belong to the WOZ estimate (section 17). Section 18 repeats the whole calculation step by step for one building, from the BAG floor area to the Estimated WOZ Value, so every figure can be checked by hand.

blocks.text: 3. The process in 10 steps
Part A - material and CO2
Read the gross floor area (GO) of the building from BAG (section 4).
Assign a building type and construction cohort, giving a material profile (section 5).
Look up the 13 material intensities of that profile in Tabel B2 (section 6).
Calculate each material mass: quantity = GO x intensity (section 7).
Calculate CO2 per material: CO2 = mass x emission factor, then add up (section 8).
Part B - Estimated WOZ Value
Find the gemeente (municipality) of the building from its postal code (section 11).
Take the base price per m2 of that gemeente from CBS (section 12).
Apply the factor for the use of the building (section 13).
Apply the factor for the age of the building (section 14).
Multiply by the floor area (GO) and round (section 15).
4. Step 1 - Gross floor area from BAG
GO is the only measured number per building. It is the sum of the usable floor area of every dwelling unit (verblijfsobject) in the pand.
5. Step 2 - Building type and cohort

The BAG use of the building is mapped to one of the seven B2 building types, and the year built to one of the four cohorts. Together they form the material_profile_id, for example EEN_1970_2000. [ASSUMED A1] - the mapping from use to B2 type is our own choice.
25 of the 28 possible profiles occur in the dataset.
6. Step 3 - B2 material intensities

7. Step 4 - Material quantity
Mi = GO x Ii and M_total = the sum of all Mi, where GO is the gross floor area (m2), Ii the intensity of material i (kg/m2 GO) and Mi the estimated mass (kg).
Over all 1,082 buildings this gives 4,335,383 tonnes, 2,043 kg per m2 of GO on average.
8. Step 5 - Embodied CO2

CO2i = Mi x EFi and CO2_total = the sum of all CO2i. [ASSUMED A3] - the emission factors are coarse working values for the production stage (A1-A3); for official Dutch reporting they should be replaced with Nationale Milieudatabase values.

blocks.text: 10. Estimated WOZ Value - overview

This part describes how the Estimated WOZ Value is calculated for the buildings in table material_estimation_final, the assumptions behind it, and one worked example. WOZ (Waardering Onroerende Zaken - valuation of real estate) is the Dutch property value used for local taxes.
[IMPORTANT] Model estimate, not an official WOZ value. Official WOZ values are set by municipalities; this estimate is not issued by or taken from a municipality, Kadaster or the Waarderingskamer.

Estimated WOZ Value = GO (gebruiksoppervlakte - usable floor area) x base EUR/m2 x type factor x age factor, rounded to the nearest € 1,000. All buildings use the same reference year: WOZ year 2026, valuation date (waardepeildatum) 2025-01-01.
11. Step 6 - Find the gemeente (municipality)
PDOK Locatieserver (location server): the postal code (postcode) of the building gives its current gemeentecode (municipality code).
If that fails: the first 4 digits of pand_id (building ID), which are the BAG gemeentecode (municipality code), if CBS still has that gemeente (municipality).
If both fail: the national CBS average (NL01 - the Netherlands).
The municipality column is not used: it comes from the notice text and holds village names and notice fragments that cannot be matched to CBS.
12. Step 7 - Base price per m2
Base EUR/m2 = CBS average WOZ value of dwellings (woningen) in the gemeente (municipality) / CBS average floor area of dwellings in the gemeente (municipality).

blocks.text: 13. Step 8 - Building type factor
The factor of the BAG gebruiksdoel (use of the building). A building with several uses gets the mean of their factors, each use counted once.
14. Step 9 - Age factor
The factor of the band that contains the bouwjaar (year built).
15. Step 10 - Floor area and final value
EUR/m2 of the building = base EUR/m2 x type factor x age factor. The estimate is the GO (gebruiksoppervlakte - usable floor area from BAG, go_m2) x EUR/m2 of the building, rounded.

blocks.text: 19. Validation

Every building is checked against GO x the B2 total intensity of its profile. 1,082 buildings were checked; 159 differ by more than 0.01 tonne, the largest difference being 2.35 tonnes, which is 0.00134% of that building's mass. The differences come from rounding in the intensity values; no value is adjusted to force a match.
20. Results - Estimated WOZ Value per building type
21. Limits
21.1 Material and CO2
The estimate scales with floor area only. A tall hall and a low hall with the same GO get the same materials.
B2 intensities are national averages per type and cohort, not the construction of the individual building.
The type mapping is coarse: assembly, healthcare, hotel, sports and education all become 'overig'.
Overige constructie mineralen dominates the mass (sand, gravel, mortar) and carries a 0.50 factor, which makes it the largest single CO2 source.
Copper, aluminium and other metal do not use the same factor in every row (section 8).
Emission factors are coarse working values; replace with Nationale Milieudatabase values for official reporting.
21.2 Estimated WOZ Value
It is a model estimate, not an official WOZ value; no official WOZ value was used to check it.
The location is only as fine as the gemeente (municipality): differences between neighbourhoods are not included.
The type and age factors are our own assumptions (B2, B4), not published values.
Mixed-use buildings weigh each use equally (B3), which overvalues a building with a small dwelling and a large shed or storage part.
Condition, finish, plot size, monument status and energy label are not included.
